t2i_prompt: A 1440 px wide desktop web section as a flat straight-on UI mockup: a warm limestone sheet inside a deep navy frame. Top left: a small wordmark and breadcrumb, then a large light-weight sans headline. Left: a three-column table of <CONTENT> with mono row numbers and hairline rules. Right: an open ring of fine radial tick marks with one big steel-blue mono numeral and unit at its centre, a single vertical limit line crossing the ring with two small outlined mono limit tags, and a small line icon of an instrument beside it. Square corners, flat, precise and calm.
signature_idea: Calibration tolerance shown as a tick-ring gauge, the figure in steel blue with its limits tagged on one vertical line.
strengths: dial readout is a strong, ownable instrument motif with one steel-blue accent
table is clean and legible with good spacing
light headline and limestone/navy palette are on-brand
weaknesses: dial reading '02%' with limits 'LMT 2 %' and '85-115 %' mixes unrelated tolerances; the gauge says nothing true
limit line cuts the ring at an arbitrary place, so the tags look decorative
invented standards and clause numbers would read as real
slightly rounded card corners break the square rule
table cells in sans, not mono figures
brand_fit_why: Navy, limestone and one steel-blue accent with a light headline and a precise dial fit the brand, but the gauge values are incoherent and corners are softly rounded.
